content:
I implemented `convert()` in `src/billing/currency.py`. It multiplies `amount_cents` by the `Decimal` rate and rounds toward negative infinity (`ROUND_FLOOR`), returning integer minor units.

I used `ROUND_FLOOR` because of the stored Treasury decision from April 2026. It keeps a conversion from crediting a customer more than the rate allows. This is deliberately different from tax rounding, which uses `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

I ran three quick checks:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| 1999 × 0.9 | 1799 |
| −1001 × 0.5 | −501 |
| 100 × 1.2345 | 123 |

The negative case rounds down to −501 rather than toward zero. That follows from the floor rule, but say if refunds or credits should round differently.

I didn't add tests or run any test suite.
